title: How Your Classroom Environment Can Improve Behavior
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that a messy, cluttered classroom quietly undermines a teacher's spoken expectations for excellent behavior and hard work, no matter how forcefully those expectations are stated aloud. He walks through several reasons a clean, organized room matters: it commands a kind of reverence from those who enter, draws students in, communicates respect for learning, calms and steadies the teacher, strengthens influence over students, projects high expectations even when the room is empty, and instills pride in students. He closes by urging teachers to spend a weekend overhauling their room, framing the environment itself as a wordless but unmistakable message that excellence is expected.
points: Treat classroom clutter as an active obstacle to behavior expectations, not just an eyesore.
Clear stacked boxes, messy work areas, and overflowing cabinets to open up walkways and desktops.
Recognize that a clean room calms and steadies the teacher as much as it does students.
Let the room's appearance signal high expectations before a word is even spoken.
Dedicate concentrated time, like a weekend, to overhauling the room rather than tackling clutter piecemeal.
quotes: A messy, unkempt, or clutter-filled classroom sends the message to your students that poor behavior and middling work habits is acceptable—regardless of how often or how forcefully you say otherwise.

Adults and students alike walk into bright, neatly arranged classrooms like they’re walking into a museum. They sort of tiptoe in, taking great care not to disturb its peacefulness and sacred learning environment.
A clutter-free classroom will have a powerful effect on you—calming you and sweeping away the mental clutter and discouragement.
In fact, your classroom environment is an uncanny predictor of how effective a teacher you are.
A sharp-dressed classroom, on the other hand—full of pride, respect, open walkways and clear desktops—is a calming, safe-haven to students—allowing them to breathe easy and focus on learning.
